executive_summary:
Episode 397 opens by framing a new Candace smear package the host nicknames Candyland: a Lisa Nose X post alleging eight illegal nannies under NDA in a second Nashville mansion, attributed originally to Jessica Reed Kraus, which the host satirizes as the latest failed character attack. She then argues a broader distraction SCOP is underway, cycling narratives (dead-internet feel) because Charlie Kirk remains unresolved: she cites Las Vegas 2017 vanishing within five days under MeToo/Harvey Weinstein coverage, then Nick Shirley's Somali-daycare scoop (and Shirley as last Charlie Kirk Show guest, booked by Andrew Kolvet) as a failed distraction, then a killer-mom / Lindsay Clancy / Nancy Mace / New York Post / Libs of TikTok filicide panic that she says neocons link to women who distrust Erika Kirk, aimed at regulating the internet after bots failed.

The core UVU beat: the independent review names a Station 2 fire captain who assisted CPR at Timpanogos Hospital but leaves him unnamed, while naming non-participants Caleb Chilcutt and Maycee Crofts. Host plays 911 audio (ladder 33 / engine 34 redirected ~12:30) and stresses that neither Frank Turek nor Brian Harpole ever mentioned a fire captain giving CPR. Frank Turek on Brandon Tatum's podcast then doubles down that Jeff Long "had the roofs," citing a Dan Flood text, after the review's release. Closing thirds cover banker whistleblower Simon Andre's reported death after flagging Howard Lutnick's Epstein ties and a 2018 email/startup claim (BBC), Zach Bryan's Free Palestine shirts and Gillette Stadium attendance-record nights after Robert Kraft canceled Macklemore, Baron Coleman under X attack after being announced as guest host during Candace's maternity leave, and comments revisiting Brian Cole Jr., Skyler, Brigitte/France, and smear economics promised for the next show.

---

claims.label: Lisa Nose tweet alleges Candace houses illegal nannies under NDA
claims.claim: On air the host reads a Lisa Nose X post claiming Candace Owens keeps eight nannies (two per child) living in a second mansion, hires nannies who are in the country illegally via an elite Jewish nanny agency, underpays them, and binds them with NDAs so they cannot speak; Nose says Jessica Reed Kraus originally reported it and that Nose confirmed via three people who know Candace.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve the original Nose and Kraus posts; seek any primary employment/immigration evidence rather than rumor chains.

claims.label: Host frames killer-mom narrative as SCOP aimed at internet regulation
claims.claim: The host argues the Lindsay Clancy-seeded, Nancy Mace / New York Post / Libs of TikTok amplified killer-mom panic is an intentional SCOP that neocons link to women who distrust Erika Kirk, and that its purpose is to justify regulating the internet after bots failed to move the public off Charlie Kirk.
claims.investigative_direction: Map amplification graphs (Mace, NY Post, Libs) against UVU-review and Charlie-case news cycles; separate statistical filicide data from narrative framing.

claims.label: Las Vegas 2017 coverage displaced within five days by MeToo / Weinstein
claims.claim: The host states the October 2017 Las Vegas mass shooting (60 dead, 869 injured; investigators cited 24 firearms in Steven Paddock's suite and no clear motive) disappeared from the media cycle in less than a week because five days later the New York Times Harvey Weinstein MeToo story broke and dominated coverage. She points to Ian Carol and others for military/Israel/Saudi conspiracy research she does not develop here.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the five-day media-shift claim against contemporary news indexes; treat Paddock/motive facts as investigator claims, not settled.

claims.label: Nick Shirley Somali daycare push failed; Shirley was last Charlie Kirk Show guest
claims.claim: The host says media tried to force the Minneapolis Somali daycare welfare scandal (broken by Nick Shirley) as a Charlie Kirk distraction weeks after the assassination, but it was not large enough; she adds Shirley was relatively unknown, had done Brazil work she will not revisit, and was the last guest on the Charlie Kirk Show, picked by Andrew Kolvet who runs Charlie's Twitter.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm Shirley appearance date/booking chain on Charlie Kirk Show; separate daycare reporting merits from distraction thesis.

claims.label: U.S. filicide is rare and majority male; epidemic framing lacks statistical basis
claims.claim: The host cites roughly 500 U.S. filicide cases per year in a nation of about 350 million (about 10% step-parents/guardians), one case per ~770,000 people, and NIH-attributed offender split of roughly 57% fathers vs 43% mothers, arguing the killer-mom epidemic framing has no basis in statistical reality.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull the NIH / official filicide statistics she paraphrases; confirm rates and sex split against primary tables.

claims.label: UVU review: Station 2 fire captain assisted CPR at hospital but is unnamed
claims.claim: The host reads the UVU independent review stating Station 3 radioed the TPUSA SUV, Station 2 rerouted to Timpanogos Hospital, and the fire captain from Station 2 assisted in providing CPR to Charlie Kirk at the hospital; she flags that this public-figure captain is unnamed while the review named Caleb Chilcutt and Maycee Crofts.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify Station 2 captain on duty 2025-09-10 via official rosters / tips (moretips@candaceowens.com); compare naming criteria in the review.

claims.label: Neither Turek nor Harpole mentions a fire captain performing CPR
claims.claim: Combining Frank Turek's claim of late-ride back-seat CPR with Brian Harpole's claim that CPR was not administered in the car (and Harpole's long hospital narrative through defibrillator prep and door guard), the host says neither man ever featured a fire captain who met them at the hospital and began CPR, which she calls an impossible dual omission given the review text.
claims.investigative_direction: Align Turek, Harpole, and review timelines minute-by-minute; seek hospital/EMS records naming the captain.

claims.label: Dispatch redirected ladder 33 and engine 34 toward Timpanogos ~12:30
claims.claim: The host plays fire dispatch audio she times around 12:30 p.m. in which ladder 33 and engine 34 are redirected toward Timpanogos, after radio traffic describing a black SUV with a person hanging out, which she presents as corroboration of the review's Station 2/3 reroute narrative.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain original Provo/Orem dispatch recordings and unit logs for ladder 33 / engine 34 / Station 2 captain assignment.

claims.label: Turek on Tatum podcast doubles down that Jeff Long had the roofs after the review
claims.claim: In a Brandon Tatum podcast clip, Frank Turek recounts a March 2026 UVU confrontation with Chief Jeff Long in which Turek cites a Dan Flood text ("I got you covered") as proof Long had the roofs, then mid-story corrects that Flood showed him the text days after the hospital rather than at the hospital; the host says Turek is still repeating roofs talking points after the independent review undercut TPUSA's security narrative.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve full Tatum interview; compare Turek's roofs claims to the published UVU review findings and Flood text metadata.

claims.label: Whistleblower Simon Andre dies after flagging Howard Lutnick Epstein ties
claims.claim: The host reports that former British banker and BGC Group managing director Simon Andre, who blew the whistle on Howard Lutnick's links to Jeffrey Epstein (including alleged island/temple visits), has died under a suicide narrative she calls remarkably suspicious; Lutnick is now U.S. Commerce Secretary, and the host ties the story to Trump/Bondi reluctance on Epstein files.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify Andre identity, death circumstances, and BBC reporting; document Lutnick's public statements on Epstein island visits.

claims.claim: Per the host's BBC-attributed account, Simon Andre said he discovered a 2018 email chain in which Howard Lutnick and Jeffrey Epstein discussed prospects of a startup business, which Andre cast as Lutnick failing to disclose a business relationship with Epstein after Epstein's Palm Beach conviction.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the BBC interview/article and any produced email exhibits; confirm dates relative to Epstein's legal status.
